claim: The Bicoid-hunchback (Bcd-hb) system in the fruit fly embryo has been used as a model to study how positional information in morphogen concentration gradients is robustly translated into step-like responses for over 40 years.
source: For over 40 years, the Bicoid-hunchback (Bcd-hb) system in the fruit fly embryo has been used as a model to study how positional information in morphogen concentration gradients is robustly translated into step-like responses.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical use of the Bcd-hb system as a research model, drawing on established scientific practice.

claim: All the early hb expression pattern features and temporal dynamics are compatible with an equilibrium model with a short decay length Bicoid activity gradient as a sole source of positional information.
source: By using the MS2-MCP RNA-tagging system and analysing in real time, the transcription dynamics of synthetic reporters for Bicoid and/or its two partners Zelda and Hunchback, we show that all the early hb expression pattern features and temporal dynamics are compatible with an equilibrium model with a short decay length Bicoid activity gradient as a sole source of positional information.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from MS2-MCP RNA-tagging system analysis of synthetic reporters.

claim: Zelda lowers the Bicoid concentration threshold required for transcriptional activation.
source: Meanwhile, Bicoid's partners speed-up the process by different means: Zelda lowers the Bicoid concentration threshold required for transcriptional activation while Hunchback reduces burstiness and increases the polymerase firing rate.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations from synthetic reporter analysis.

claim: Hunchback reduces burstiness and increases the polymerase firing rate.
source: Meanwhile, Bicoid's partners speed-up the process by different means: Zelda lowers the Bicoid concentration threshold required for transcriptional activation while Hunchback reduces burstiness and increases the polymerase firing rate.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations from synthetic reporter analysis.

claim: The Bcd gradient was shown to be steadily established at the onset of transcription, one hour after egg laying, in the form of an exponential AP gradient with a λdecay length measured in the range of 16–25% egg-length (EL).
source: The Bcd gradient was shown to be steadily established at the onset of transcription, one hour after egg laying, in the form of an exponential AP gradient with a λdecay length measured in the range of 16–25% egg-length (EL) (Abu-Arish et al., 2010; Durrieu et al., 2018; Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies that measured the Bcd gradient.

claim: Fluorescent correlation spectroscopy measurements and single molecule tracking of GFP-tagged Bcd proteins revealed that a fraction of the Bcd proteins has a fast diffusion coefficient sufficient to explain the establishment of the gradient in such a short time by the synthesis-diffusion-degradation model.
source: Fluorescent correlation spectroscopy measurements (Abu-Arish et al., 2010) and single molecule tracking of GFP-tagged Bcd proteins (Mir et al., 2018) revealed that a fraction of the Bcd proteins has a fast diffusion coefficient sufficient to explain the establishment of the gradient in such a short time by the synthesis-diffusion-degradation model (Abu-Arish et al., 2010; Fradin, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies using fluorescent correlation spectroscopy and single molecule tracking.

claim: The establishment of the Bcd gradient is extremely precise in space with only 10% variability among embryos.
source: Of note, the establishment of the Bcd gradient is not only rapid but also extremely precise in space with only 10% variability among embryos (Gregor et al., 2007b) and the gradient is linearly correlated to the amount of bcd mRNA maternally provided and the number of functional bcd alleles in the females (Liu et al., 2013; Petkova et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gregor et al., 2007b.

claim: The Bcd gradient is linearly correlated to the amount of bcd mRNA maternally provided and the number of functional bcd alleles in the females.
source: Of note, the establishment of the Bcd gradient is not only rapid but also extremely precise in space with only 10% variability among embryos (Gregor et al., 2007b) and the gradient is linearly correlated to the amount of bcd mRNA maternally provided and the number of functional bcd alleles in the females (Liu et al., 2013; Petkova et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2013 and Petkova et al., 2014.

claim: The Bcd protein binds DNA through its homeodomain.
source: The Bcd protein binds DNA through its homeodomain (Hanes and Brent, 1989; Treisman et al., 1989) and activates the expression of a large number of target genes carrying Bcd binding sites (BS).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hanes and Brent, 1989 and Treisman et al., 1989.

claim: Among the Bcd target genes, hunchback (hb) is expressed in a large domain spanning the whole anterior half of the embryo.
source: Among the Bcd target genes, hunchback (hb) is expressed in a large domain spanning the whole anterior half of the embryo (Driever et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Driever et al., 1989.

claim: hb expression begins when the first hints of transcription are detected in the embryo, i.e. at nuclear cycle 8.
source: hb expression begins when the first hints of transcription are detected in the embryo, i.e. at nuclear cycle 8 (Porcher et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Porcher et al., 2010.

claim: At nuclear cycle 14, the expression domain of hb is delimited by a posterior boundary, which is both precisely positioned along the AP axis and very steep.
source: About one hour later (i.e. at nuclear cycle 14), the expression domain of hb is delimited by a posterior boundary, which is both precisely positioned along the AP axis and very steep suggesting that very subtle differences in Bcd concentration in two nearby nuclei at the boundary are already precisely measured to give rise to very different transcriptional responses (Crauk and Dostatni, 2005; Gregor et al., 2007a; Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Crauk and Dostatni, 2005; Gregor et al., 2007a; Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002.

claim: Transcription at the hb locus is detected during the successive S-phases but not during the intervening mitoses.
source: Detailed analysis of hb expression by RNA FISH also indicated that transcription at the hb locus is extremely dynamic in time: it is detected during the successive S-phases but not during the intervening mitoses, which punctuate this period of development.
evidence: This claim is based on RNA FISH analysis data.

claim: The hb-P2 MS2-reporter is expressed anteriorly in a domain with a boundary of the same steepness and positioning precision as the endogenous hb.
source: This provided an hb-P2 MS2-reporter expressed anteriorly in a domain with a boundary of the same steepness and positioning precision as the endogenous hb (Lucas et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lucas et al., 2018.

claim: At the single locus level, the variability in the total mRNA production (δmRNA/mRNA) over an entire nuclear cycle for loci at the boundary was of 150%.
source: Of note, despite, this highly reproducible measurement of positional information (position and steepness of the boundary) on the scale of the embryo, at the single locus level, the variability in the total mRNA production (δmRNA/mRNA) over an entire nuclear cycle for loci at the boundary was of 150 %, i.e. one locus can produce 2.5 X more mRNA than another locus (Desponds et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Desponds et al., 2016.

claim: The high variability in mRNA production reflects a stochastic transcription process in neighboring nuclei which nevertheless all make the precise decision to turn ON hb during the cycle.
source: This high variability (noise) was consistent with smFISH data measuring the variability of hb mRNA amounts in nuclei (Little et al., 2013). It reflects a stochastic transcription process in neighboring nuclei which nevertheless all make the precise decision to turn ON hb during the cycle.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from variability data and supported by citation to Little et al., 2013.

claim: The transcription dynamics of the hb-P2 MS2-reporter indicated that its steep boundary is established at each nuclear cycle 11–13 within 180 s.
source: The transcription dynamics of the hb-P2 MS2-reporter indicated that its steep boundary is established at each nuclear cycle 11–13 within 180 s and therefore suggested that accurate measurements of Bcd concentration were made much more rapidly than anticipated (Lucas et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lucas et al., 2018.

claim: Inactivating Bcd by optogenetics in the embryo indicated that the hb transcription exhibited a very fast sensitivity to Bcd activity.
source: Consistently, inactivating Bcd by optogenetics in the embryo indicated that the hb transcription exhibited a very fast sensitivity to Bcd activity (Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2017.

claim: A model assuming cooperative binding of Bcd proteins to the six known BS sites of the hb-P2 promoter and rate limiting concentrations of Bcd at the boundary was able to recapitulate the fast temporal dynamics of the boundary establishment but could not reproduce its observed steepness.
source: Modeling was used to recapitulate the observed dynamics assuming cooperative binding of Bcd proteins to the six known BS sites of the hb-P2 promoter and rate limiting concentrations of Bcd at the boundary (Tran et al., 2018a). The model was able to recapitulate the fast temporal dynamics of the boundary establishment but could not reproduce its observed steepness which, given the 20% EL decay length of the Bcd protein gradient measured with immuno-staining (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002), corresponds to a Hill coefficient of ~7, difficult to achieve without invoking the need for additional energy expenditure (Estrada et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to modeling studies (Tran et al., 2018a; Estrada et al., 2016) and measurement data (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002).

claim: The performance of the model was higher when increasing the number of Bcd BS above six with a minimum of 9 Bcd BS required to fit the experimental data with a boundary of the appropriate steepness.
source: As expected, the performance of the model was higher when increasing the number of Bcd BS above six with a minimum of 9 Bcd BS required to fit the experimental data with a boundary of the appropriate steepness.
evidence: This claim is based on modeling results and comparison to experimental data.

claim: Six Bcd BS are not sufficient to recapitulate the hb-P2 expression dynamics.
source: We show that 6 Bcd BS are not sufficient to recapitulate the hb-P2 expression dynamics while a reporter with only 9 Bcd BS recapitulates most of its spatial features, except a slightly lower steepness of its expression boundary and a longer period to reach steady state.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from synthetic reporters.

claim: A reporter with only 9 Bcd BS recapitulates most spatial features of hb-P2, except a slightly lower steepness of its expression boundary and a longer period to reach steady state.
source: We show that 6 Bcd BS are not sufficient to recapitulate the hb-P2 expression dynamics while a reporter with only 9 Bcd BS recapitulates most of its spatial features, except a slightly lower steepness of its expression boundary and a longer period to reach steady state.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from synthetic reporters.

claim: The bursty behavior of Bcd-only reporters in excess of Bcd is accounted for by a model involving a first step of Bcd binding/unbinding to the BS array and a second step where the bound Bcd molecules activate transcription.
source: To account for the bursty behavior of Bcd-only reporters in excess of Bcd, we fitted our data to a model involving a first step of Bcd binding/unbinding to the BS array and a second step where the bound Bcd molecules activate transcription.
evidence: This claim is based on model fitting to experimental data.

claim: Zld sites contribute to the first step of the model by drastically lowering the Bcd concentration thresholds required for activation.
source: Synthetic reporters combining Bcd BS with either Hb or Zld BS indicated that both Hb and Zld sites reduce the time to reach steady state and increase expression by different means: Zld sites contribute to the first step of the model by drastically lowering the Bcd concentration thresholds required for activation while Hb sites act in the second step by reducing Bcd-induced burstiness and increasing the polymerase firing rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from synthetic reporters with Zld binding sites.

claim: Hb sites act in the second step by reducing Bcd-induced burstiness and increasing the polymerase firing rates.
source: Synthetic reporters combining Bcd BS with either Hb or Zld BS indicated that both Hb and Zld sites reduce the time to reach steady state and increase expression by different means: Zld sites contribute to the first step of the model by drastically lowering the Bcd concentration thresholds required for activation while Hb sites act in the second step by reducing Bcd-induced burstiness and increasing the polymerase firing rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from synthetic reporters with Hb binding sites.

claim: In embryos maternally expressing one (1 X) vs two (2 X) bcd functional copies, the boundary shift of the Bcd-only synthetic reporter with 9 Bcd BS was small enough to set the Bcd system within the limits of an equilibrium model.
source: Importantly, in embryos maternally expressing one (1 X) vs two (2 X) bcd functional copies, the boundary shift of the Bcd-only synthetic reporter with 9 Bcd BS was small enough to set the Bcd system within the limits of an equilibrium model.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing 1X and 2X bcd embryos.

claim: The shift observed for the hb-P2 reporter in 1 X vs 2 X bcd backgrounds was the same as for the synthetic reporters.
source: Lastly, the shift observed for the hb-P2 reporter in 1 X vs 2 X bcd backgrounds was the same as for the synthetic reporters further supporting that the Bcd gradient is the main source of positional information for the early expression of hb.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing hb-P2 and synthetic reporters in different bcd backgrounds.

claim: The expression of the B6, B9, and B12 reporters harbored similar features as expression of the hb-P2 reporter.
source: The expression of the B6 (6 Bcd BS), B9 (9 Bcd BS), and B12 (12 Bcd BS) reporters harbored similar features as expression of the hb-P2 reporter (Lucas et al., 2018), which carries the ~300 bp of the hb-P2 promoter and the hb intron (Figure 1B, Supplementary file 1, Video 4): during the cycle, transcription was first initiated in the anterior with the expression boundary moving rapidly toward the posterior to reach a stable position into nc13 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and comparison to Lucas et al., 2018.

claim: Bcd concentration is a rate-limiting factor for the expression of all reporters.
source: Thus, Bcd concentration is a rate-limiting factor for the expression of all reporters.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that T0 depends on position along the AP axis.

claim: The time it took for the hb-P2 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary was only 225 ± 25 s.
source: This contrasts to the middle of the axis where the absolute number of Bcd molecules has been evaluated to be around 700 (Gregor et al., 2007a) and where the Bcd protein is thus likely to be limiting: transcription dynamics of the various reporters was quite diverse (Figure 1F) and the time it took for the hb-P2 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary (converging time, Supplementary file 2) was only 225 ± 25 s while it took about twice as much time for B6 (425 ± 25 s) or B9 (475 ± 25 s) and slightly less for B12 (325 ± 25 s).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and Supplementary file 2, with citation to Gregor et al., 2007a.

claim: The time it took for B6 to reach the final decision to position its boundary was 425 ± 25 s.
source: This contrasts to the middle of the axis where the absolute number of Bcd molecules has been evaluated to be around 700 (Gregor et al., 2007a) and where the Bcd protein is thus likely to be limiting: transcription dynamics of the various reporters was quite diverse (Figure 1F) and the time it took for the hb-P2 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary (converging time, Supplementary file 2) was only 225 ± 25 s while it took about twice as much time for B6 (425 ± 25 s) or B9 (475 ± 25 s) and slightly less for B12 (325 ± 25 s).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and Supplementary file 2.

claim: The time it took for B9 to reach the final decision to position its boundary was 475 ± 25 s.
source: This contrasts to the middle of the axis where the absolute number of Bcd molecules has been evaluated to be around 700 (Gregor et al., 2007a) and where the Bcd protein is thus likely to be limiting: transcription dynamics of the various reporters was quite diverse (Figure 1F) and the time it took for the hb-P2 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary (converging time, Supplementary file 2) was only 225 ± 25 s while it took about twice as much time for B6 (425 ± 25 s) or B9 (475 ± 25 s) and slightly less for B12 (325 ± 25 s).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and Supplementary file 2.

claim: The time it took for B12 to reach the final decision to position its boundary was 325 ± 25 s.
source: This contrasts to the middle of the axis where the absolute number of Bcd molecules has been evaluated to be around 700 (Gregor et al., 2007a) and where the Bcd protein is thus likely to be limiting: transcription dynamics of the various reporters was quite diverse (Figure 1F) and the time it took for the hb-P2 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary (converging time, Supplementary file 2) was only 225 ± 25 s while it took about twice as much time for B6 (425 ± 25 s) or B9 (475 ± 25 s) and slightly less for B12 (325 ± 25 s).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and Supplementary file 2.

claim: For all reporters, the fraction of nuclei with MS2 signal during the cycle exhibited a sigmoid-like pattern along the AP axis reaching 100% in the anterior and 0% in the posterior.
source: For all reporters, the fraction of nuclei with MS2 signal during the cycle exhibited a sigmoid-like pattern along the AP axis reaching 100% in the anterior and 0% in the posterior (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Increasing the number of Bcd BS from 6 to 9 shifted the expression boundary toward the posterior and decreased the width of the boundary.
source: Increasing the number of Bcd BS from 6 to 9, shifted the expression boundary toward the posterior and decreased the width of the boundary (Figure 1H), whereas increasing the number of Bcd sites from 9 to 12 did not significantly change the boundary position nor the boundary width.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Increasing the number of Bcd sites from 9 to 12 did not significantly change the boundary position nor the boundary width.
source: Increasing the number of Bcd BS from 6 to 9, shifted the expression boundary toward the posterior and decreased the width of the boundary (Figure 1H), whereas increasing the number of Bcd sites from 9 to 12 did not significantly change the boundary position nor the boundary width.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: B9, B12, and hb-P2 expression boundaries were at almost identical positions.
source: Of note, B9, B12, and hb-P2 expression boundaries were at almost identical positions while the width of the hb-P2 boundary was smaller than the width of the B9 or the B12 boundaries (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The width of the hb-P2 boundary was smaller than the width of the B9 or the B12 boundaries.
source: Of note, B9, B12, and hb-P2 expression boundaries were at almost identical positions while the width of the hb-P2 boundary was smaller than the width of the B9 or the B12 boundaries (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The burstiness observed in the anterior is not caused by the binding/unbinding of Bcd to the BS array but by downstream processes.
source: As in this region the Bcd BS on those reporters are likely to be always occupied by Bcd molecules, the burstiness observed is not caused by the binding/unbinding of Bcd to the BS array but by downstream processes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that burstiness persists even when Bcd is in excess.

claim: A H6 reporter containing only 6 Hb BS did not exhibit any MS2 signal from nc11 to nc13.
source: A H6 reporter containing only 6 Hb BS did not exhibit any MS2 signal from nc11 to nc13 (not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: The Hb protein alone, even with an abundance of Hb sites, could not activate transcription on its own.
source: This indicated that the Hb protein alone, even with an abundance of Hb sites, could not activate transcription on its own.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that H6 reporter did not show MS2 signal.

claim: The presence of Hb BS reduced to 325 ± 25 s the time required for the synthetic H6B6 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary.
source: Interestingly, at their respective boundary positions where the Bcd concentration is limiting, the presence of Hb BS reduced to 325 ± 25 s the time required for the synthetic H6B6 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary (purple dashed line in Figure 3E and converging time, Supplementary file 2) when it was 425 ± 25 s for B6 (yellow dashed line in Figure 3E and converging time, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Supplementary file 2.

claim: For H6B6, the boundary was slightly (only one nucleus length) shifted toward the posterior and the width was reduced by half when compared to B6.
source: For H6B6, the fraction of nuclei with MS2 signal during the cycle exhibited a sigmoid-like pattern (Figure 3F) with, when compared to B6, a boundary slightly (only one nucleus length) shifted toward the posterior and a width reduced by half (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F and 3G.

claim: In the anterior region, the fraction of loci's active time at steady state was always near saturation for the H6B6 reporter (~0.95–1).
source: In the anterior region, this fraction was always near saturation for the H6B6 reporter (~0.95–1) (Figure 3H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), with very few nuclei exhibiting bursty expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The non-bursty behavior of the H6B6 reporter contrasts with the highly bursty expression of B6 reporter.
source: This non-bursty behavior of the H6B6 reporter contrasts with the highly bursty expression of B6 reporter (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the anterior region, the mean fluorescence intensity of active H6B6 loci was at least twice higher than that of all synthetic Bcd-only reporters.
source: Meanwhile, in the anterior region, the mean fluorescence intensity of active H6B6 loci was at least twice higher than that of all synthetic Bcd-only reporters (Figure 3I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Hb binding to the promoter accelerates the measurement of positional information by Bcd by improving both the unbinding kinetics of Bcd to its BS and the kinetics of activation/deactivation transcription rates.
source: Altogether, this suggests that Hb binding to the promoter accelerates the measurement of positional information by Bcd by improving both the unbinding kinetics of Bcd to its BS, which is consistent with the half reduction of the boundary steepness (Figure 3G) and the kinetics of activation/deactivation transcription rates, consistent with reduced burstiness (Figure 3H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental observations and model fitting results.

claim: A reporter with only 6 Zld BS (Z6) was strongly expressed along the whole AP axis.
source: As a reporter with only 6 Zld BS (Z6) was strongly expressed along the whole AP axis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), we had to reduce the number of Zld BS in our synthetic approach to analyze Zld effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A Z2 reporter containing only 2 Zld BS did not exhibit any MS2 signal.
source: A Z2 reporter containing only 2 Zld BS did not exhibit any MS2 signal (not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: Zld binding can accelerate Bcd-dependent transcription when Bcd is rate-limiting but has no effect when Bcd is in excess.
source: This suggests that Zld binding can accelerate Bcd-dependent transcription when Bcd is rate-limiting but has no effect when Bcd is in excess (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that Z2B6 onset time does not vary along AP axis.

claim: The presence of Zld BS reduced to 300 ± 25 s the time required for the synthetic Z2B6 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary.
source: As observed with H6B6, the presence of Zld BS reduced to 300 ± 25 s the time required for the synthetic Z2B6 reporter to reach the final decision to position its boundary (blue dashed line in Figure 3E and converging time, Supplementary file 2) when it was 425 ± 25 s for B6 (yellow dashed line in Figure 3E and converging time, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Supplementary file 2.

claim: The most striking feature of the Z2B6 reporter was the drastic posterior shift of its expression boundary by ~17.5 %EL when compared to B6.
source: The most striking feature of the Z2B6 reporter was the drastic posterior shift of its expression boundary by ~17.5 %EL when compared to B6 (Figure 3, C-D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: The threshold of Bcd concentration required for activation is lowered when two Zld BS are present in the promoter together with 6 Bcd BS.
source: It indicates that the threshold of Bcd concentration required for activation is lowered when two Zld BS are present in the promoter together with 6 Bcd BS.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the posterior shift of Z2B6 boundary.

claim: Zld binding to the promoter accelerates the measurement of positional information by Bcd by facilitating Bcd binding when it is rate-limiting through an increase of the Bcd binding rate kb, without affecting the kinetics of activation/deactivation transcription rates.
source: Altogether, this suggests that Zld binding to the promoter accelerates the measurement of positional information by Bcd by facilitating Bcd binding when it is rate-limiting through an increase of the Bcd binding rate kb, without affecting the kinetics of activation/deactivation transcription rates.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental observations and model fitting results.

claim: Embryos from wild-type females (2 X) express quantitatively twice as much Bcd proteins as embryos from Δbcd/ + females (1 X).
source: As the amount of Bcd protein is produced from each bcd allele independently of any other allele in the genome (Liu et al., 2013) and as changing the genetic dosage of bcd in the female leads to proportional changes in both mRNA and protein number in the embryo (Petkova et al., 2014), we assumed that embryos from wild-type females (2 X) express quantitatively twice as much Bcd proteins as embryos from Δbcd/ + females (1 X).
evidence: This claim is based on citations to Liu et al., 2013 and Petkova et al., 2014.

claim: The comparison of hb-P2 patterns in Bcd-2X vs Bcd-1X embryos indicated a shift of 11.0% ± 0.5%EL of the expression boundary.
source: Lastly, the comparison of hb-P2 patterns in Bcd-2X vs Bcd-1X embryos indicated a shift of 11.0% ± 0.5%EL of the expression boundary (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The shift obtained for the hb-P2 MS2 reporter was significantly larger than the shift of 8% EL described for hb in previous studies using the bcdE1 allele.
source: Of note, the shift obtained for the hb-P2 MS2 reporter was significantly larger than the shift of 8% EL described for hb in previous studies using the bcdE1 allele (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002; Porcher et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison to previous studies cited (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002; Porcher et al., 2010).

claim: In embryos from wild-type vs bcdE1/ + females, the shift of boundary position was 8% EL.
source: To understand this discrepancy, we measured the shift in the boundary positions of our hb-P2 and synthetic MS2 reporters in embryos from wild-type vs bcdE1/ + females and confirmed that in this genetic background the shift of boundary position was 8% EL (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, panel B-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The bcdE1 allele likely allows the expression of a weakly functional truncated protein.
source: As the molecular lesion in the bcdE1 allele introduces a premature stop codon downstream of the homeodomain (Struhl et al., 1989), these results suggest that the bcdE1 allele likely allows the expression of a weakly functional truncated protein.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the discrepancy in shift measurements and citation to Struhl et al., 1989.

claim: Lowering the decay length of the Bcd gradient to its effective value allows a more reliable fit of the model to the data and places back the Bcd system within the physical limits of an equilibrium model for concentration sensing.
source: Thus, lowering the decay length of the Bcd gradient to its effective value allows a more reliable fit of the model to the data and places back the Bcd system within the physical limits of an equilibrium model for concentration sensing.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the model fitting results.

claim: Zld functions as a pioneer factor by potentiating chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding and gene expression of the targeted promoter.
source: Zld functions as a pioneer factor by potentiating chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding and gene expression of the targeted promoter (Foo et al., 2014; Harrison et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Foo et al., 2014 and Harrison et al., 2011.

claim: Zld has been shown to bind nucleosomal DNA.
source: Zld has recently been shown to bind nucleosomal DNA (McDaniel et al., 2019) and proposed to help establish or maintain cis-regulatory sequences in an open chromatin state ready for transcriptional activation (Eck et al., 2020; Hannon et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to McDaniel et al., 2019, Eck et al., 2020, and Hannon et al., 2017.

claim: Zld is distributed in nuclear hubs or microenvironments of high concentration.
source: In addition, Zld is distributed in nuclear hubs or microenvironments of high concentration (Dufourt et al., 2018; Mir et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dufourt et al., 2018 and Mir et al., 2018.

claim: Bcd has been shown to be distributed in hubs even at low concentration in the posterior of the embryo.
source: Interestingly, Bcd has been shown to be also distributed in hubs even at low concentration in the posterior of the embryo (Mir et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mir et al., 2017.

claim: Bcd hubs are Zld-dependent.
source: These Bcd hubs are Zld-dependent (Mir et al., 2017) and harbor a high fraction of slow moving Bcd molecules, presumably bound to DNA (Mir et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mir et al., 2017 and Mir et al., 2018.

claim: Hb synergizes with Bcd in the early embryo.
source: In contrast to Zld, our knowledge on the mechanistic properties of the Hb protein in the transcription activation process is much more elusive. Hb synergizes with Bcd in the early embryo (Simpson-Brose et al., 1994) and the two TF contribute differently to the response with Bcd providing positional and Hb temporal information to the system (Porcher et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Simpson-Brose et al., 1994 and Porcher et al., 2010.

claim: Bcd provides positional and Hb temporal information to the system.
source: In contrast to Zld, our knowledge on the mechanistic properties of the Hb protein in the transcription activation process is much more elusive. Hb synergizes with Bcd in the early embryo (Simpson-Brose et al., 1994) and the two TF contribute differently to the response with Bcd providing positional and Hb temporal information to the system (Porcher et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Porcher et al., 2010.

claim: Hb contributes to the determination of neuronal identity later during development.
source: Hb also contributes to the determination of neuronal identity later during development (Hirono et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hirono et al., 2017.

claim: Hb is one of the first expressed members of a cascade of temporal TFs essential to determine the temporal identity of embryonic neurons in neural stem cells (neuroblasts) of the ventral nerve cord.
source: Interestingly, Hb is one of the first expressed members of a cascade of temporal TFs essential to determine the temporal identity of embryonic neurons in neural stem cells (neuroblasts) of the ventral nerve cord.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about Hb function in neuroblasts.

claim: Hb is not able to activate transcription on its own but strongly increases RNAP firing probability and burst length of a locus licensed to be ON.
source: Our work indicates that Hb is not able to activate transcription on its own but that it strongly increases RNAP firing probability and burst length of a locus licensed to be ON.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations from this study.

claim: When comparing the transcription patterns of the B9 reporter in Bcd-2X flies and Bcd-1X flies, a shift of ~10.5 ± 1% EL of the boundary position was detected.
source: When comparing the transcription patterns of the B9 reporter in Bcd-2X flies and Bcd-1X flies, we detected a shift of ~10.5 ± 1% EL of the boundary position.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: This shift revealed a gradient of Bcd activity with an exponential decay length of ~15 ± 1.4% EL (~75 µm).
source: This shift revealed a gradient of Bcd activity with an exponential decay length of ~15 ± 1.4% EL (~75 µm), significantly smaller than the value observed directly (20% EL, ~ 100 µm) with immuno-staining for the Bcd protein gradient (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002) but closer from the value of 16.4% EL obtained with immuno-staining for Bcd of the Bcd-GFP gradient (Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is based on calculation from experimental data and comparison to previous studies (Houchmandzadeh et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2013).

claim: The effective decay length of 15% EL may correspond to a population of 'active' or 'effective' Bcd distributed in steeper gradient than the Bcd protein gradient observed by immunodetection.
source: Our work opens the possibility that the effective decay length of 15% EL corresponds to a population of 'active' or 'effective' Bcd distributed in steeper gradient than the Bcd protein gradient observed by immunodetection which would include all Bcd molecules.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Bcd molecules have been shown to be heterogenous in intranuclear motility, age and spatial distributions.
source: Bcd molecules have been shown to be heterogenous in intranuclear motility, age and spatial distributions but to date, we do not know which population of Bcd can access the target gene and activate transcription (Tran et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tran et al., 2020.

claim: The existence of two (or more) Bicoid populations with different mobilities raises the question of the underlying gradient for each of them.
source: The existence of two (or more) Bicoid populations with different mobilities (Abu-Arish et al., 2010; Fradin, 2017; Mir et al., 2018) obviously raises the question of the underlying gradient for each of them.
evidence: This claim is based on citations to studies showing Bcd heterogeneity (Abu-Arish et al., 2010; Fradin, 2017; Mir et al., 2018).

claim: The dense Bcd hubs persist even in the posterior region where the Bcd concentration is low.
source: Also, the dense Bcd hubs persist even in the posterior region where the Bcd concentration is low (Mir et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mir et al., 2017.

claim: As the total Bcd concentration decreases along the AP axis, the hubs accumulate Bcd with increasing proportion in the posterior, resulting in a steeper gradient of free-diffusing Bcd molecules outside the hubs.
source: As the total Bcd concentration decreases along the AP axis, these hubs accumulate Bcd with increasing proportion in the posterior, resulting in a steeper gradient of free-diffusing Bcd molecules outside the hubs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation about Bcd hubs.

claim: The gradient of newly translated Bcd was found to be steeper than the global gradient.
source: At last, the gradient of newly translated Bcd was also found to be steeper than the global gradient (Durrieu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Durrieu et al., 2018.

claim: A smaller decay length means that the effective Bcd concentration decreases faster along the AP axis.
source: Of note, a smaller decay length also means that the effective Bcd concentration decreases faster along the AP axis.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the definition of decay length.
